title: Cap. X: controversy-aim — show the eternal distinction of elect and non-elect in God's mind and will had no origin or motive from antecedent foresight of good acts in Peter/Paul or opposite acts in Cain/Judas
pass_a_gloss: About to dispute therefore concerning this decree of reprobation, we shall do this one thing, that it may be shown that that everlasting distinction of the elect and non-elect in the Divine mind and will had not origin, occasion, or any motive whatsoever from antecedent foresight of good acts in the elect persons, namely of penitence, faith, and perseverance in Peter and Paul, and from antecedent foresight of opposites in the non-elect, to wit of impenitence, unbelief, and final contumacy in Cain, Judas, and the rest; but that the mere will of God first divided between sons infallibly ordained unto participation of grace and of glory, and between the rejected or those passed over as to such an order.
pass_b_english: So in disputing this reprobation decree we shall do one thing: show that the eternal distinction of elect and non-elect in God's mind and will had no origin, occasion, or motive of any kind from antecedent foresight of good acts in the elect — penitence, faith, and perseverance in Peter and Paul — or from antecedent foresight of the opposites in the non-elect — impenitence, unbelief, and final contumacy in Cain, Judas, and the rest. Rather, God's mere will first divided between sons infallibly ordained to share grace and glory, and those rejected or passed over as to that order.
source_text: De hoc igitur reprobationis decreto disputaturi, id unum agemus, ut ostendatur, Aeternam illam distinctionem electorum et non-electorum in mente et voluntate Divina non habuisse originem, occasionem, aut motivum qualecunque ex antecedanea praevisione bonorum actuum in personis electis, puta poenitentiae, fidei et perseverantiae in Petro et Paulo, et ex antecedanea praevisione oppositorum in non-electis, scilicet impoenitentiae, infidelitatis et contumaciae finalis in Caino, Juda, reliquisque; sed meram Dei voluntatem primo divisisse inter filios ad participationem gratiae et gloriae infallibiliter ordinatos, et inter rejecticios sive quoad talem ordinem praeteritos.
